vulnerabilities.description: Jackson Core's async parser can accumulate excessively long digit sequences (~20,000x amplification of the intended maxNumberLength limit) when input is fed in small chunks without a terminator, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on maxNumberLength.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a reactive/async network-facing service that parses untrusted JSON with this parser. Track upstream fix (2.18.8 / 2.21.4 / 2.22.1) for the next dependency refresh.

ratings.justification: Client-side use only, against trusted cloud-provider endpoints; no attacker-controlled JSON is parsed via the vulnerable non-blocking parser API.

analysis.detail: Incomplete fix for a prior number-length constraint bypass: Jackson's async/non-blocking parser (NonBlockingJsonParser / ByteArrayFeeder) silently buffers digit characters up to maxStringLength instead of enforcing maxNumberLength when input arrives in small chunks without a terminator byte. Found in jackson-core 2.22.0 bundled into liquibase-aws-extension.jar and liquibase-azure.jar. Both extensions are outbound clients that call AWS/Azure APIs and parse the responses those services return over TLS; neither extension's own code invokes Jackson's non-blocking parser API, and neither exposes a network-facing endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled JSON. Exploiting this would require an attacker already able to forge or MITM AWS/Azure API responses, at which point far more direct attacks are already available.
